## Title

## Caption (Instagram)

```
9pm isn't a coincidence — it's the busiest minute on your street. Wifi is radio sharing the same air, and the pipe into your flat is shared too. Three fixes in the video. Save it for tonight.
```

## YouTube Shorts

**Title:** Why your wifi dies at nine pm

**Description:**

```
9pm isn't a coincidence — it's the busiest minute on your street. Wifi is radio sharing the same air, and the pipe into your flat is shared too. Three fixes in the video. Save it for tonight.

Sources:
- Wifi operates in unlicensed radio bands shared by many devices and networks. (Wi-Fi / RF Spectrum Use Guidelines (Cornell IT)) https://it.cornell.edu/wifi/wi-fi-rf-spectrum-use-guidelines-cornell-university checked 2026-10-28
- In the 2.4 GHz band there are only three non-overlapping channels: 1, 6 and 11. (Wi-Fi / RF Spectrum Use Guidelines (Cornell IT)) https://it.cornell.edu/wifi/wi-fi-rf-spectrum-use-guidelines-cornell-university checked 2026-10-28
- Neighbouring networks compete for the same limited set of non-overlapping channels. (Wi-Fi / RF Spectrum Use Guidelines (Cornell IT)) https://it.cornell.edu/wifi/wi-fi-rf-spectrum-use-guidelines-cornell-university checked 2026-10-28
- The 5 GHz band offers many more non-overlapping channels than 2.4 GHz. (Wi-Fi / RF Spectrum Use Guidelines (Cornell IT)) https://it.cornell.edu/wifi/wi-fi-rf-spectrum-use-guidelines-cornell-university checked 2026-10-28
```
